Reference.Title: Applications of Nasal High-Flow Oxygen Therapy in Critically ill Adult Patients
Reference.Address: [Porhomayon, Jahan] SUNY Buffalo, Sch Med & Biomed Sci, Div Crit Care Med, VA Western New York Healthcare Syst,Dept Anesthes, Buffalo, NY USA; [El-Solh, Ali A.; Jaoude, Philippe] SUNY Buffalo, Sch Med & Biomed Sci, Div Pulm Crit Care & Sleep Med, VA Western New York Healthcare Syst,Dept Med, Buffalo, NY USA; [Pourafkari, Leili] SUNY Buffalo, Dept Anesthesiol, Buffalo, NY USA; [Nader, D.] SUNY Buffalo, Sch Med & Biomed Sci, Div Cardiothorac Anesthesia & Pain Med, VA Western New York Healthcare Syst,Dept Anesthes, Buffalo, NY USA; [Porhomayon, Jahan] VA Med Ctr, Rm 203C,3495 Bailey Ave, Buffalo, NY 14215 USA
Reference.Abstract: The use of nasal high-flow oxygen therapy (NHFOT) has become increasingly common in hospitals across Europe, Asia, and North America. These high utility devices provide an efficient and comfortable access points for providing supplemental oxygen to patients with variety of respiratory disorders. They are relatively easy to set up, and clinicians and patients alike give very positive feedback about their ease of use and comfort for patients in the hospital setting. However, it remains uncertain whether NHFOT improves patient survival or even reduces respiratory complications. Outcome data in adult populations are few and frequently underpowered to guide physicians for their widespread use in hospital setting. In this article, we present a review of the current technology and available studies pertinent to NHFOT.
